fields.meta_title: RSVP Form Builder for Any Event | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an RSVP form that counts plus-ones, caps seats with a waitlist, and lets guests change a reply from their own link. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an RSVP Form That Counts Plus-Ones and Caps Seats
fields.hero_description: Build an RSVP form that counts every yes and plus-one, closes at your cap, and saves each reply to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Happens After a Guest Says Yes
fields.features_subheading: The count on the reply-by date is what an RSVP form is for. Emergent builds the form, the guest list, and the rules behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Plus-ones counted in the total

Decide which guests may bring someone. A yes with a plus-one adds two to the headcount, and the companion's name goes on the same reply, so the door list matches the count.
fields.feature_2:
A seat cap that starts a waitlist

Set the number of seats the room holds. Once that many guests say yes, later replies join a waitlist in order, and a guest who backs out frees a seat for the next one.
fields.feature_3:
Replies guests can change themselves

Each guest gets a personal link to their own reply. A guest can switch from yes to no, add a companion, or fix a misspelled name, and the host never has to edit the list by hand.
fields.feature_4:
Follow-up questions only for a yes

Ask about allergies, arrival time, or parking only after a yes. Guests who decline answer one question and leave, and the host reads the answers as totals per question.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before the reply-by date

Pick a reply-by date and when to nudge the quiet ones. The app emails guests who have not answered, and on the deadline it sends the host the final count with plus-ones.
fields.feature_6:
The guest list stays in your database

Every reply is a row in a database you own, with no response cap. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, so next year's event can start from this one.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (SurveyMonkey, Jotform, Typeform, Canva), RSVP tools and a Reddit thread asking for a free RSVP link: every result helps a host collect a yes or a no, and none shows what happens to the count after that. This page covers the general event RSVP (office parties, member previews, kids' birthdays, charity galas) and the parts that keep a headcount right: plus-ones counted in the total, a seat cap with a waitlist, replies guests can change from their own link, follow-up questions that appear only after a yes, and table hosts who name their own guests. Wedding household lookups and meal choices stay on the wedding RSVP page, and paid or timed signups go to the event booking form.
tab_stories: Tamsin Hoek invites 142 people to the Strandquist Freight holiday party; 96 say yes and 21 of them bring a plus-one, 31 say no and 15 never reply, and on the Dec 5 reply-by date the app emails her a headcount of 117 to send the caterer.

Dovecote Arts Center caps its members' preview at 80 yeses and holds 9 people on a waitlist; when Ilse Faraji changes her reply to No from her own link, Orrin Strandquist, first on the waitlist, gets her spot and a confirmation email, and the waitlist drops to 8.

Ines Duvernay-Pike invites 18 kids to Pip's 8th birthday at Crestline Climbing; 14 say yes, 3 say no and 1 has not replied, and the yes replies list 2 nut allergies, 1 dairy allergy and 5 parents who will stay.

Saltmeadow Food Bank sells its gala by the table of 8; table host Constance Ferreira-Ng has named 6 of her 8 guests, and the app emails her on Oct 23 to name the last 2 before the Oct 30 seating deadline.
